sources.citation: Brown, Jason & Melissa Irvine. 2021. Avaipa, a Language of Central Bougainville. Oceanic Linguistics 60(1): 1-35. doi:10.1353/ol.2021.0000
sources.note: Section 4.1 Phonology (pp. 8-9) gives only the consonant and vowel inventories, the syllable template (C)(C)V(V)(C) and permitted codas [p, r, s, n]; nothing on word stress, tone or prosody for Avaipa. The single occurrence of 'stress' is footnote 2 (p. 2), which concerns Naasioi, not Avaipa: 'as pointed out by Hurd and Hurd (1970), stress is on the first vowel of the name, and since stress falls on the second syllable of words, this implies a long vowel' (justifying the spelling 'Naasioi').
